Replay

Replay Duel

11 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Browser match invitationsNative provisioned matchesBrowser play and acceptanceAuthenticated P2P admission

Run this two-player projectile duel to study peer-to-peer (P2P) simulation. Both participants simulate the complete match and exchange inputs; neither sends authoritative world corrections. Deterministic execution lets them compare state hashes after receiving the same inputs. The original games remain separate.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/play.sh
RDP_ROLE=dial nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/play.sh

nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/resume_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/rejoin_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/watch_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/profile_run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_deterministic/run.sh

Start the two interactive commands in separate terminals. A/D move, Space jumps, and J fires. The default role listens; RDP_ROLE=dial connects to localhost. Port defaults to 49520. This initial launcher admits one remote ENet peer and binds the listening/dialing roles to fixed logical IDs 1/2. Fresh ENet connection IDs can therefore change during coordinated restore. Production admission/rendezvous is not implemented by that native ENet launcher. The browser invitation path below uses durable provisioning and authenticated rendezvous.

Browser match invitations#

Run the separate Duel service, export/serve the browser game, and open lobby.html. Under Match invitations, supply the service address and choose Create match. The game offers Invite player before the other participant arrives. Share that link with a different browser profile/device, which chooses Join match. Credentials are generated and saved automatically in each profile's IndexedDB; only the bearer invitation goes in the shared link. The invitation dialog supports both browser-native Copy and manual selection.

Before closing a participant, use Save & pause and keep the downloaded file. To return, open the lobby with the same service, import that file and choose Rejoin recent. Enrollment alone cannot restore the simulation/input history. The service registers a newer process incarnation while retaining the match's session and ordered player IDs. Both the creator and guest can use this flow; compatible participant history is still required.

The flow uses the reusable P2P party owner. The service fixes the roster at two players and grants no simulation authority. A guest can wait for the creator's signaling room for up to 15 seconds. Initial enrollment/registration failures remain explicit; established gameplay does not stop solely because the enrollment control connection fails.

Shell
REPLAY_P2P_PARTY_OUT=/absolute/fresh/build nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_party/run.sh
REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 REPLAY_P2P_PARTY_OUT=/absolute/fresh/build \
REPLAY_P2P_PARTY_RUN=/absolute/fresh/creator-return REPLAY_P2P_PARTY_MODE=creator \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_party/run.sh

This browser path uses WebRTC. Native two-player provisioning uses encrypted ENet through P2P Direct. Public accounts/deployment and authenticated spectator enrollment remain open. The direct demo, manually issued credential fixtures and native ENet scenarios remain independently runnable.

Native provisioned matches#

Use the same Duel service with native RDP_PARTY=create, join, or rejoin and RDP_SERVICE=wss://your-service. A private CA can be supplied with RDP_CA. Explicit loopback development uses RDP_LOCAL=1 with a loopback WS service. RDP_ADDRESS/RDP_PORT advertise the local native endpoint. The creator listens; the guest discovers the creator's current registered endpoint through the service. Optional RDP_BIND_ADDRESS/RDP_BIND_PORT select the local listener independently for interface/port forwarding. Omitting both retains the advertised endpoint as the listener. The service still receives only the advertised endpoint.

Create on one profile/device and use Copy invitation. The joining profile supplies that code as RDP_INVITE. Set RDP_ROOMS_DB and RDP_ARCHIVE to separate absolute paths when testing multiple native profiles on one machine. Defaults use the game's user directory. The enrollment database and participant archive are different files.

To return after Save & pause, use the same database with RDP_PARTY=rejoin, RDP_STAGE=resume and the saved RDP_ARCHIVE. A creator can register a new port; the survivor follows the new endpoint after authenticating the new incarnation. The original RDP_ROLE/direct ENet demonstration remains available when RDP_PARTY is absent. Native provisioned mode currently supports two participants.

Shell
REPLAY_P2P_NATIVE_OUT=/absolute/fresh/build nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_native/run.sh
REPLAY_P2P_NATIVE_OUT=/absolute/fresh/build REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 \
REPLAY_P2P_NATIVE_RUN=/absolute/fresh/guest REPLAY_P2P_NATIVE_MODE=guest \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_native/run.sh

The model in shared/duel uses Q24.8 coordinates, checked updates, stable projectile slots and frame-owned RNG. Three hits kill a fighter; respawn happens after a deterministic randomized delay. All bullets resolve before damage is applied so same-tick trades are symmetric. Presentation draws copied state and uses an event journal to reconcile displayed effects after replay.

The real-process gate uses 120 ms receive delay per side, 0–20 ms jitter, 10% unreliable loss and 10% duplication. It simulates 600 ticks, waits for both confirmed checksums, verifies the whole final world against a reference run and checks shot event reconciliation. The default two-tick input delay and eight-tick prediction limit intentionally expose stalls at this latency. A stall counter counts attempted steps that waited, not distinct simulation ticks or elapsed stall duration.

tests/replay_deterministic executes a 2,400-tick corpus with four seeds on native arm64 and freestanding WASM, comparing canonical state/event hashes and gameplay counters. The WASM module imports no host simulation functions. This is execution evidence, not merely a type-check. Separate browser tests exercise P2P gameplay and coordinated file recovery. Other native targets and polished lobby/recovery UX remain pending.

resume_run.sh saves each participant's full protocol archive at tick 240 while the final ticks are still speculative. It kills both processes, creates new ENet connections, restores their different durable frontiers and continues to tick 600. The gate checks the full world and shot journal against uninterrupted execution. Use REPLAY_KEEP_LOGS=1 to retain the logs and .rply files. To inspect a saved participant without Godot or a network:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/verify.sh /path/to/listen.rply

The verifier reexecutes the retained inputs and checks every state/event digest. tests/replay_p2p/run.sh creates normal and deliberately divergent recordings, executes the same verifier on native arm64 and WASM, and requires the changed execution to first mismatch at tick 12. This is a bounded retained history, not a full-length replay movie. See the archive contract.

rejoin_run.sh exercises a native live rejoin. Only the dialing participant saves at tick 240 and is killed. The listener stays in the same process, stalls at its prediction bound and waits through timeout. A fresh dialing process restores its own file; the listener rebinds its logical peer to the new ENet connection and calls p2p.reconnect. The gate verifies that the listener's current frame, captured input frontier, confirmed tick and timeline allocation survive the rebind, then checks both tick-600 worlds and shot journals against uninterrupted execution. Set RDP_REJOIN_OUT to an empty directory to choose retained output. RDP_LIVE_REJOIN=1 (browser ?live_rejoin=1) enables this fixture's reconnect behavior. The browser lobby enables it; direct launch defaults remain off.

The fixed loopback role mapping is a trusted test provider, not authenticated admission. Old ENet identities are excluded by the replacement mapping. The saved participant stops sampling before it is killed: an arbitrary older archive can fail if survivors have inputs it forgot or required retransmission history was evicted. The runner refuses both cases. The same behavior has a browser test described below. Authenticated browser creator recovery also has a separate gate.

creator_rejoin_run.sh covers the native listening participant returning. The creator saves and pauses at tick 240, then is killed. The dialing process retains its runner through timeout, closes its retired transport and reconnects to the restored listener at the same address. Physical server ID 1 is reused, so an explicit transport-reopen state triggers the logical rebind. The gate checks the world, sampled/confirmed and receive/ACK frontiers, local slot, roster, chain and input/hash/timeline storage, then compares both tick-600 worlds and shot journals with uninterrupted execution. Use RDP_CREATOR_OUT for a fresh output directory. This replaces a listening transport, not a missing participant's input history; the same archive-retention limits and trusted loopback-provider scope apply.

watch_run.sh adds a third Godot process after confirmed tick 150. Its separate spectator connection receives only confirmed history. A six-second blackout of that connection allows the two players to advance beyond retained history; the spectator reports the omitted range, rebuilds at a new baseline, and continues through tick 900 with new shot events and the same reference world. The gate requires at least 128 ticks of post-recovery play. It uses the same delay/jitter/ loss profile as the player fixture. Disable the blackout with RDP_WATCH_BLACKOUT_MS=0 to exercise continuous late-join delivery.

For interactive spectating, start the listening player with RDP_WATCH=1, start the dialing player normally, then start a third play.sh with RDP_ROLE=watch. The spectator connects to game port + 1. The current launcher admits one viewer and trusts the listening participant as the viewing source. Spectators are independent of the player roster; losing their connection cannot stall players. watch_failover_run.sh closes only that spectator stream during active play, then reconnects the viewer to the second participant on game port + 2. A retained anchor proves continuity, so the viewer keeps its world and event journal and reaches tick 900 without another presentation reset. Both players keep simulating. The native fixture uses configured loopback peers and a private anchor file. It does not establish public authenticated spectator provisioning, browser source-switch integration, automatic restoration of a restarted spectator, or delayed disclosure; those still need implementation or integration. See the spectator contract.

View geometry was copied from Replay Quickdraw's script-free gunner/bullet scenes; see its original asset provenance. The copied fighter scene SHA-256 is 7ccb2b812b16da493fb2157206da86b18b9d21e28b95f0d39df87055bbf7fb24; the bullet is f1d1339990e8adfec1e7861831a18e17177b6e0959abb10e7812b15b022b7777. These are provisional views; human visual/play-feel review remains open.

The profiling contract explains operation wall timings and capture-to-first-simulation latency. profile_run.sh compares two/eight delay ticks with the same gameplay inputs; tests/replay_p2p/bench.sh separately measures optimized native process CPU over two peers and Memory transport. tests/replay_deterministic/run.sh checks default and speed optimization on the host and WASM, plus macOS x86-64 under Rosetta when available. Rosetta validates an alternate ISA binary on this Mac, not independent x86 hardware or other OSes. Set REPLAY_REQUIRE_ROSETTA=1 to make an unavailable Rosetta check fail explicitly.

Browser play and acceptance#

Shell
# Build/export, start the local signaling/HTTP fixtures and print the lobby URL.
REPLAY_WEB_PLAY=1 nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/web_run.sh

# Automated separate-Chrome-process scenarios; logs are retained.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_duel/web_run.sh

The lobby creates a match or joins a room as a player/spectator. The hosting game shows room codes and copy buttons for join/watch links. A/D, Space and J drive the same inputs as native play. Browser ?role=, ?url=, ?room= and other lowercase query names correspond to native RDP_ROLE, RDP_URL, RDP_ROOM, etc. The default browser backend is raw Replay WebRTC; the native backend remains ENet. Neither path uses Godot scene RPCs. Two trusted participants bind to fixed logical IDs 1/2. Numeric transport IDs and copied links do not authenticate a player.

A viewer joins a separate watch room, corresponding to native's separate watch port. It is outside the player confirmation roster. The full suite covers:

  • fault: 600 ticks with 120 ms receive delay, 20 ms jitter, 10% unreliable loss and duplication, plus a three-second input blackout. Prediction reaches its bounded horizon and waits, then retransmission/rollback reaches the reference.
  • watch: a third browser joins after tick 150. Six seconds of lost spectator traffic exceed retained history; an explicit reset resumes viewing, with at least 128 further ticks before the 1,200-tick reference/effect checks.
  • resume: both participants export their own 240-tick protocol archives. The driver verifies downloaded file lengths and closes both browser processes. Fresh browsers import those files through the lobby, open a fresh RTC room and restore their different durable input frontiers before continuing to tick 600.
  • rejoin: the dialing browser clicks Save & pause during play. The driver verifies the downloaded file and that its head and sampled frontier stop, then kills that Chrome process. The match creator stays open through timeout. A fresh browser imports the file and joins the same room with a new physical RTC ID; the survivor retains its frame/allocation and both reach the tick-600 reference.
  • creator (authenticated provider): the creator clicks Save & pause and its browser is killed. The joining browser stays open through timeout. A fresh creator imports its own file and credential; peer ID 1 receives a new connection generation. The survivor retains its runner and both reach tick 600.
  • interactive: actual keyboard movement/jump/fire reaches the other browser; the hosting page's copy button produces the expected join link.

Select scenarios with REPLAY_WEB_MODES="fault watch"; choose a retained log location with REPLAY_DUEL_WEB_LOGS=/absolute/path. There are no automatic retries. The delay/loss decorator runs at the application's packet boundary over real WebRTC; this does not emulate internet NAT, packet-level SCTP congestion or TURN.

Browser recovery uses explicit participant files, with a 16 MiB import bound. The lobby finishes an IndexedDB upload transaction before entering the game; the game waits for the bounded buffer and performs normal archive decoding and reexecution validation. Initiating a browser download does not prove it was saved: the browser/user owns completion. This test verifies actual files and restores in new browser processes. It does not claim implicit Godot virtual-filesystem flush durability.

To leave and return as the joining player, click Save & pause, keep the completed download, and close that browser. Leave the match creator open. To return, open its join link, import your participant file and join the room. Save & pause stops new input capture while servicing received inputs and presentation reconciliation; there is no continue button that could silently make the downloaded file stale. For an authenticated fixed match, the creator can also save and return while the joining browser stays open: import its own credential and archive, then create the same match again. The service retains the fixed match scope. The plain local signaling fixture still requires coordinated recovery when its creator closes. The signaling service must remain available for either live-rejoin flow.

The local fixture is not an authenticated public relay. STUN/TURN deployment, additional browser engines, source failover, and automatic coordinated save/lobby flows remain open. Human play-feel review is still needed. Recorded browser evidence includes logs, archives and rendered views. The live browser rejoin evidence records the killed process, survivor identity, archive and state checks.

Authenticated P2P admission#

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_admission/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_admission/service_run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_p2p_admission/web_run.sh

The browser test starts a native Godot signaling provider with a fixed two-member registry. Each Chrome process imports its personal JSON credential using the lobby's credential input; the file contains member, incarnation and a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal key. The lobby stores only that participant's credential in its tab's sessionStorage and carries auth=1 in navigation/join links. Keys never appear in the URL. The authenticated profile currently admits players only.

Duel opens Rtc_P2P_Auth using its session/content/epoch and ordered member IDs 1/2. Before initial binding and live rejoin it requires the provider's verified member identity for the connected physical RTC peer. The gate rejects a duplicate creator, wrong key, wrong role, unknown member and replayed connection proof, then saves and kills only the dialing browser. Its authenticated replacement receives a new RTC ID, restores its archive and reaches the tick-600 reference with the live survivor.

The fixture uses published test credentials and loopback WS. A deployment must issue personal credentials and authenticate the provider, for example through verified WSS. This fixture does not provide a public Party account/invite flow or authenticated spectator admission. Native listening-transport replacement has the separate loopback gate above. The browser gate covers either participant returning, including a creator whose numeric RTC ID remains 1 while its connection generation changes. See the provider contract and recorded evidence.
